title: ORIANNA: An Accelerator Generation Framework for Optimization-based Robotic Applications
problem: Existing accelerator approaches for optimization-based robotic applications either fail to exploit sparse structures inherent in robotic algorithms or require expensive manual design of dedicated hardware. These limitations lead to both performance inefficiencies and prohibitive non-recurring engineering costs.
motivation: Optimization-based robotic applications require efficient hardware acceleration while reducing the high engineering costs of manual accelerator design.
method: ORIANNA is an automated accelerator generation framework that synthesizes hardware designs optimized for optimization-based robotic workloads. The framework exploits sparse structure patterns common in robotic algorithms through systematic architecture generation rather than manual design, reducing NRE costs.
key_novelty: Automatic hardware accelerator synthesis specifically optimized for sparse structures in optimization-based robotic applications.
contributions: Automated accelerator generation framework for optimization-based robotic algorithms
Exploitation of sparse computational patterns through framework-based synthesis
Significant reduction in non-recurring engineering costs versus manual accelerator design
limitations: Specific performance metrics, baseline comparisons, and generalization beyond optimization-based robotic workloads not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Automated accelerator generation for sparse robotic optimization
